clue.text: Penny-pinching firm

explanation.definitionFit: A miser is called close-fisted, and a knot that will not slip is secure; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Two money, prizes put up of the highest quality

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a reward is a prize of money
a pot is the money prize in a game of cards

explanation.surface: Two cash prizes are offered for the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns REWARDPOT backwards, read upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for top class or of the highest social standing.

clue.text: Tawdry celebrations in college

definitions.meaning: an annual feast held for old members at an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy means flashy, while in Oxford colleges a gaudy is a reunion dinner for alumni.

clue.text: Diminutive chap, one favouring offensive weapon

parts.note: Tom is a short form of Thomas, as in Tom Thumb
a means one
a hawk is someone favouring aggressive military action

explanation.surface: A small man who backs aggressive action wields a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon by Native Americans.

clue.text: Resented impolite cut-off -—- asked — to go outside

indicators.note: the word for asked is told to surround the other piece, so it is split open around it

parts.note: to ask for something is to beg for it

indicators.note: cut off means the word for impolite loses its final letter

parts.note: impolite means rude

explanation.surface: Someone resented being cut off rudely and then asked to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'cut-off' reads as a rude interruption but is the trimming signal on impolite, and 'to go outside' asks the begging word to surround that trimmed piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something is to resent it, so the past tense swaps for resented.

clue.text: City in which one can keep clean

definitions.meaning: a historic spa city in Somerset, England

definitions.text: in which one can keep clean
definitions.meaning: a tub for washing the body

explanation.definitionFit: Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman baths, and a bath is a tub for washing.

clue.text: Skiers will usually deteriorate

definitions.meaning: the way skiers normally travel is down a slope

explanation.definitionFit: Literally skiers descend slopes; idiomatically something in decline is said to be heading the same way.

clue.text: Water spirit appearing surprisingly in nude

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A water nymph appears unexpectedly naked.
explanation.definitionFit: An undine is a female water sprite in folklore, made famous by Paracelsus and Fouqué.

clue.text: Long ago landing up in prison, tiresome person given one

indicators.note: in puts the turned tiresome person inside the prison

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for a tiresome person is read upward

parts.note: a pill is a boring, tiresome person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tiresome ends up landing in prison along with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long ago landing' is the definition, recalling the 1915 Allied landings; 'up' turns the dull person upward in this down entry before 'in' places it inside the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allied landings at Gallipoli in 1915 were a famous First World War campaign.

clue.text: Murder, followed by good thrashing

indicators.note: followed by means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: to do in is slang for to murder

explanation.surface: A killing, then a good beating afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A doing is British slang for a beating or thrashing.

clue.text: Fallen fruit handed out

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
to mete out is to hand out or allot

explanation.surface: Fruit that has dropped from the tree is being distributed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plummeted means dropped sharply, a synonym of fallen in the past-participle sense.

clue.text: Henry is employed in food shop in capital

indicators.note: being employed in a shop means working inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry works in a delicatessen in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person but is the electrical unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi (strictly New Delhi) is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Upfront rationalisation helped you to have more time

indicators.note: upfront means at the front, so the leading letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Thinking things through in advance helped you gain more time.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, time means the rhythmic pattern or metre, as in keeping time.

clue.text: Royal bird, royal and swaggering

parts.note: in Britain the swan is the royal bird, traditionally owned by the monarch
a king is a royal person

explanation.surface: A regal swan with a royal air struts about proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: Unmarked mute swans on open water in England belong to the Crown, hence the royal bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To swank is to show off, so swanking is swaggering or showing off.

clue.text: Top of hat, new bowler, might be seen here

parts.note: the crown is the top part of a hat
green means new or inexperienced

explanation.surface: The crown of a hat, perhaps a new bowler hat, is on view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' looks like the hat but is someone playing bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown green is a bowling green with a raised centre, where bowls players compete.

clue.text: How sun moves in front of house? That's novel

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece is placed before the second

parts.note: the sun crosses the sky from east to west, moving westward

explanation.surface: Asking how the sun travels across the front of a house, then calling it new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective but is the definition: Westward Ho! is a novel by Charles Kingsley.
explanation.definitionFit: Westward Ho! is an 1855 novel by Charles Kingsley, giving its name to a Devon village.

clue.text: Makeshift bed, as he'd know, needs making up

indicators.note: making up means the letters are composed anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A temporary bed, as anyone would know, must be made.
explanation.definitionFit: A shakedown is an improvised bed made up on the floor.

clue.text: Second person no longer working in TV drama

parts.note: an OAP, old-age pensioner, is a retired person

explanation.surface: A retired actor plays a secondary role in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is the British abbreviation for old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial television drama.

clue.text: A way to carry money box containing cents, not new

indicators.note: the money box is to hold cents in place of the letter for new, which is not there

parts.note: a piggy bank is a child's money box

explanation.surface: A money box with some coins in it, but not brand new, is a way to carry it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing cents, not new' swaps the N of PIGGYBANK for C.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a piggyback means carrying them on your back.

clue.text: Man has a fling in airport

parts.note: he refers to a man
to fling is to throw

explanation.surface: A man has an affair at an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' suggests a romance but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's main international airport.

clue.text: Author hasn't finished book

indicators.note: not finishing means the author's surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth

explanation.surface: A writer has left a book unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is a noun here: a good book is a good read.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a read is something to read, so a good book is called a good read.

clue.text: Roll about in grass, getting unpleasantly hot

indicators.note: in places the word for rolling about inside the word for grass

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, and so is to sing
to welter is to roll or wallow about

explanation.surface: Someone rolls around on the lawn and becomes uncomfortably hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is not the lawn but British slang for informing, which criminals also call singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweltering describes weather or a person oppressively, uncomfortably hot.

clue.text: Have difficulty breathing in this joint.

definitions.meaning: a stuffy, smothering condition that makes breathing hard
the joint in a horse's hind leg corresponding to the knee

explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to smother, and the stifle is the knee joint of a horse's hind leg.

clue.text: Standing around, for instance, after priest is taken ill

indicators.note: after means the turned abbreviation is placed following the anagram
being taken ill suggests the word priest is upset and rearranged
around means the abbreviation for for instance is turned back to front

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: People stand around, for example, after a priest falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken ill' signals the priest's letters going awry, and 'around' turns the Latin abbreviation back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is standing or reputation in the eyes of others.

clue.text: Song son had in hand

indicators.note: to have something in is to hold it inside, so the son goes within

parts.note: the palm is the inner part of the hand

explanation.surface: A son held a song in his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song, especially from the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Awkward, in a way — disgusting

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
icky means nasty or disgusting

explanation.surface: Something awkward and, in a sense, rather revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is an awkward or difficult one.

clue.text: Break the ice left in grotto

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the grotto

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: Someone breaks the ice they left in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break the ice' suggests social awkwardness, but a glacier calves when ice breaks off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaciers and ice sheets are said to calve when chunks break off into the sea.

clue.text: Broadcast unusual item

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A strange item is put on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or broadcast a signal.

clue.text: Unfriendly little boy given money

parts.note: Al is a short form of a boy's name such as Alan or Albert
oof is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A small boy is handed some cash and becomes standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof is distant and cool, so unfriendly in manner.

clue.text: Victor's character revealed as medals are dished out

indicators.note: dishing something out scatters it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Medals are handed out and some winner's true nature shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner of medals but is Victor Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is a leading character in Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Cash, about a thousand, given to loony for a goober

indicators.note: about means the word for cash goes around the thousand

parts.note: cash is money
K stands for a thousand, from kilo
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: Money and a thousand more handed to a madman in exchange for a peanut.
explanation.walkthrough: Goober is the American Southern word for a peanut.
explanation.definitionFit: A goober is a peanut in the American South, and a monkey nut is a peanut in its shell.

clue.text: Demolish with care

parts.note: to reck is an old word meaning to care or heed

explanation.surface: Instructions to knock something down carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck a building is to destroy it, so a synonym of demolish.
